bc_single_malt.blurb: Single Malt is a stand-alone boulder in the Beachside zone of the Arrow Lake bouldering, in British Columbia's West Kootenay. It holds five problems, and the range is gentle: one at the easiest end, three around V2 and a single V4 at the top. The rock is solid gneiss, and the short line-up works well as a warm-up round or a first outing for newer boulderers. A cairned trail climbs steeply through trees to the block from the road, a few minutes on foot. The lake level matters for some of the neighbouring blocks, but this one sits uphill from the shore.

bc_jumping_frog_wall.blurb: Jumping Frog Wall is a small tier of rounded, pillowy volcanic rock on Quadra Island, in the Chinese Mountains cliffs just below the South Peak lookout. It has five climbs: four bolted sport lines and one top-rope, graded from 5.8 to 5.10. The wall is steep and strenuous, with a weathered, textured surface and wide views over the water. Look for a big dead pine standing on the ledge at its base. It sits at the right-hand end of a mossy ramp under the Great Wall buttress, so expect a bit of uphill hiking and slippery ground when wet. A helmet is a good idea.

bc_the_camel.blurb: The Camel is a rock formation on the ridge just east of Crown Mountain's main summit, in the North Shore Mountains above North Vancouver. It reaches roughly 1,480 m and is treated as a mountaineering objective more than a cragging destination. There are five routes: a scramble-grade line, one around 5.6, and three around 5.9, mixing trad, a top-rope and one alpine route. Expect exposed scrambling with serious consequences for a fall, and plan for a rope, helmet and rappel gear. It suits climbers comfortable on mountain terrain rather than beginners.
